abstract: Inside Higher Ed's July 7, 2026 rolling monthly tracker of June 2026 higher-ed cost-cutting: UMinn eliminated 230 jobs and cut ~$44M; Johns Hopkins laid off ~110 employees concentrated in the Bloomberg School of Public Health, Carey Business School, and central administration; The New School cut 87 (19 professors, 68 staff); Southern Oregon University eliminated 66 positions and shuttered three academic programs.
keyFindings: UMinn: 230 jobs eliminated through layoffs and attrition; $44M budget cut
Johns Hopkins: ~110 layoffs concentrated in Bloomberg School, Carey Business School, central admin
The New School: 87 employees laid off (19 professors, 68 staff)
Southern Oregon University: 66 positions cut (23 faculty, 43 staff); three academic programs shuttered
Johns Hopkins driver: 'hundreds of millions of dollars in federal funding' lost since January 2025
methodology: Journalistic aggregation of institutional announcements and public filings during June 2026, part of Inside Higher Ed's rolling monthly cost-cutting series.
qualifiers: Cuts driven primarily by federal funding loss (Trump administration policy changes), enrollment declines, and general budget pressure — AI is a secondary factor at best. Frame as funding + AI, not AI-only.
